overall_safety_summary: The scene shows a person slicing tomatoes on a cutting board next to a stove, presenting risks from a protruding pot handle and unsafe finger placement during cutting.

hazards.description: The handle of the pot on the stove is turned outward to the right, protruding into the active counter workspace.
hazards.explanation: An outward-facing pot handle can easily be bumped or snagged by the user's arm, potentially knocking the pot over.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults with reduced peripheral vision or slower reflexes are at a higher risk of accidentally bumping protruding handles.
hazards.recommended_action: Turn the pot handle inward so it does not protrude over the edge of the stove or into the workspace.

hazards.description: The user is holding the tomato with flat, extended fingers close to the knife blade instead of using a claw grip.
hazards.explanation: Slicing round, slippery food items with extended fingers increases the risk of the knife slipping and causing a finger injury.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults may have reduced hand strength or tremors, making precise knife control more difficult and increasing the risk of cuts.
hazards.recommended_action: Curl the fingers inward into a claw grip to protect fingertips while stabilizing the tomato.

uncertainties: It is unclear if the pot on the stove is currently hot or contains liquid.
It is uncertain if there is a non-slip mat underneath the wooden cutting board to prevent it from sliding.
